source_caption:
When Toy Story premiered in 1995, it made history as the world’s first fully computer-animated feature film. More than two decades later, Toy Story 4 showcased just how far animation technology had evolved.

The difference is remarkable. From the simpler textures, lighting, and character models of the original film to the incredibly detailed environments of Toy Story 4, every frame reflects years of innovation. Realistic fur, floating dust particles, natural shadows, and stunning environmental detail bring the world to life in ways that were unimaginable when the first film was released.

What’s even more impressive is that the animation became so advanced that some scenes looked almost too real. Director Josh Cooley revealed that the team occasionally had to reduce the realism to maintain the stylized look that defines the Toy Story universe.
